correctness.rationale: The Dulac factor B=1/(xy) differentiates to −r/(ky)+a/(x+b)²−σ/x, strictly negative for σ≥a/(4b), including equality by (x+b)²≥4bx. Conversely for any σ below cutoff choose k>3b and sufficiently small r with e∈(0,1), then y*=2rb(k−b)/(ak), d=ea/2−σy*>0. The predator nullcline slope strictly exceeds the prey nullcline slope across the rising range, so their only positive intersection is x=b; the Jacobian trace and determinant are positive by the strict k,r choices. Boundedness, positive invasion at (k,0), invariant boundary axes and unstable unique interior equilibrium allow Poincaré–Bendixson to produce a positive periodic orbit. Independently checked the exact rational example: x*=1, y*=29/1500, trace 19/30000, determinant 2233/1875000, and verified the Dulac identity algebraically. No uniqueness or stability of cycles is claimed.
residual_risks: Existence relies on analytic planar Poincaré–Bendixson, not symbolic diagnostics; result uniform only when other parameters are free.
